failure_analysis.what: Aligned Uint32Array SWAR word loop regressed from baseline 1.623 to median 1.590 (-2.0%)
failure_analysis.why: Per-iteration alignment check overhead exceeded word-loop benefit. The alignment check `((base + i) & 3) === 0` plus division `(base + i - aOff) / 4` runs on every iteration of the infinite for(;;) loop, but alignment is rare after the first few bytes of a string. The existing 4x byte-reject loop (round 2) already handled most strings efficiently; adding the word loop in front added branch misprediction and arithmetic overhead without sufficient payoff. After processing a single byte through the byte path, the position becomes misaligned and stays misaligned for 1-3 iterations, meaning the alignment check fails repeatedly.
failure_analysis.lesson: Hot-path checks must be nearly-free or guarded by cheaper predicates. A per-iteration branch that usually fails adds more cost than an occasionally-slower fallback. The 4x unrolled byte loop was already near-optimal for typical string content (spaces, digits, letters all >0x5c); word-level SWAR only wins when strings are long AND aligned AND contain mostly high bytes, which is rare in JSON. Future attempts should either: (1) align once at string entry and stay aligned throughout, or (2) only check alignment after consuming a full cache line, not every 4 bytes.
